introduction_markdown: Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1½ hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question (Section II: answer ALL questions, choosing one question from each pair of alternatives). For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State two factors that affect the pressure exerted by liquids. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Determine the total pressure at a point $10\,\mathrm{m}$ below the surface of a lake. Assume that atmospheric pressure is $1.0\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa}$ and the density of the lake water is $1025\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The pressure exerted by a liquid depends on (any two): the **depth** $h$ below the surface; the **density** $\rho$ of the liquid; the acceleration of free fall $g$. It does not depend on the shape or the cross-sectional area of the container.

(ii) Pressure due to the water: $P_{water} = h\rho g = 10\times 1025\times 10 = 1.025\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa}$.

Total pressure = atmospheric pressure + pressure due to the water:

$P = 1.0\times10^{5} + 1.025\times10^{5} = 2.025\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa} \approx 2.0\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: State Hooke's law and name a material that obeys the law. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Hooke's law:** the extension of a material (for example a spring or a wire) is directly proportional to the applied force (load), provided the elastic limit is not exceeded. Mathematically $F = ke$, where $k$ is the force constant.

**Material that obeys the law:** a steel spring (also a copper wire or a steel wire), within its elastic limit.
